details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the mod_http2 module of the Apache HTTP Server (httpd), the standard web server used across Red Hat Enterprise Linux and other products. HTTP/2 allows a client to send many requests at the same time over a single connection, and the module handles these concurrent requests using multiple threads. Due to a thread-safety flaw, one thread can modify memory that belongs to another thread, corrupting the server's internal memory. A remote attacker who can reach the web server could exploit this flaw to execute arbitrary commands on the server without any authentication, potentially leading to a complete takeover of the affected system, unauthorized access to sensitive data, and service disruption. Only servers that have HTTP/2 enabled are affected; servers configured to serve only HTTP/1.1 are not vulnerable.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: httpd:2.4/mod_http2: mod_http2: httpd: Remote code execution in mod_http2
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The Red Hat Product Security team has assessed the severity of this vulnerability as Critical. It allows unauthenticated remote code execution, and public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit against a default-configured server with the mod_http2 module enabled. Successful exploitation allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands, gain full control of the server process, and access or modify sensitive information.

The vulnerability's root cause is a thread-safety flaw in the mod_http2 module's handling of concurrent HTTP/2 requests: a worker thread writes into memory owned by the connection thread through a shared, lock-free allocator. This issue affects servers with HTTP/2 (h2 or h2c) enabled via the Protocols directive; servers serving only HTTP/1.1 are not affected.

Because exploitation depends on HTTP/2 stream workers sharing an allocator with the connection, the severity of this flaw varies across Red Hat products. The mod_http2 packages shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 allocate each HTTP/2 stream from a separate allocator, which substantially increases the complexity of exploiting the flaw. The severity for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 is therefore rated Important rather than Critical. Versions of mod_http2 prior to 2.0.8 do not contain the affected code, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier are not affected. Refer to the affected packages table for the severity assigned to each Red Hat product.

HTTP/2 allows a client to send many requests at the same time over a single connection, and the module handles these concurrent requests using multiple threads. notes.text: httpd:2.4/mod_http2: mod_http2: httpd: Remote code execution in mod_http2
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:

It allows unauthenticated remote code execution, and public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit against a default-configured server with the mod_http2 module enabled. Successful exploitation allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands, gain full control of the server process, and access or modify sensitive information.

notes.text:
An update for krb5 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Kerberos is a network authentication system, which can improve the security of your network by eliminating the insecure practice of sending passwords over the network in unencrypted form. It allows clients and servers to authenticate to each other with the help of a trusted third party, the Kerberos key distribution center (KDC).

Security Fix(es):

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests (CVE-2026-112323)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup (CVE-2026-112322)

* krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries (CVE-2026-112314)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request (CVE-2026-71200)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths (CVE-2026-112321)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching (CVE-2026-112320)

* krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd (CVE-2026-107884)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation (CVE-2026-112319)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers (CVE-2026-112318)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path (CVE-2026-112317)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding (CVE-2026-119079)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure (CVE-2026-112316)

* krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification (CVE-2026-111423)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure (CVE-2026-112315)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests (CVE-2026-107708)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials (CVE-2026-107778)

* krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container (CVE-2026-71199)

* krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure (CVE-2026-118380)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun (CVE-2026-107364)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* auth_gssapi_wrap_data xdr_bytes failure leak [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296016)

* xdr_bytes() does not free its allocation on partial decode failure [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296028)

* RPCSEC_GSS context lifecycle leaks [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296038)

* xdr_krb5_principal decode leak [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296050)

* process_chpw_request leak [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296060)

* Read overruns in GSSRPC svcauth_unix [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296071)

* Null dereference in KDC dispatch corner case [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296084)

* KDC DoS based on otherName value in PKINIT SAN code [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296100)

* Memory leak on krb5 gss_accept_sec_context() failure [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296117)

* KDC authdata filter does not catch KDC-issued types nested inside AD-IF-RELEVANT containers [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296132)

* Null dereference of principal names in krb5_rd_cred() [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-297005)

* Dereference of empty first credential list element in GSS mechanism [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-297013)

* Fix validation issues for trusted inputs [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299756)

* Skip expired keys when iterating over KEYRING ccache [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299758)

* Pass through null deleg_cred from SPNEGO to mech [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299759)

* Fix leaks on error in PKINIT signed-data creation [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299760)

* Fix hex key input handling in ktutil addent [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299761)

* Check reply length before V4 reply check [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299762)

* Fix memory leak in mpool_get() error paths [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299763)

* json: Correctly abort parse on invalid array [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299764)

* Prevent unsigned int overflow in iakerb_save_token() [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299765)

* Fix ksu memory leak in fcmd_resolve() [rhel-9.8.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299766)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to a complete denial of service across the authentication realm. In default Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations, PKINIT pre-authentication is not activated; exploitation strictly requires the administrator to have explicitly enabled PKINIT via `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` in the KDC configuration. Deployments operating with standard Kerberos authentication mechanisms and without PKINIT configured are unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable PKINIT on the KDC if certificate-based authentication is not required, or restrict network access to the KDC service using firewall rules.

1. Disabling PKINIT:
Edit `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf` and comment out or remove the `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` directives within the realm configuration:
```
# pkinit_identity = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.pem,/etc/krb5kdc/kdckey.pem
# pkinit_anchors = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/cacert.pem
```

Apply the changes by restarting the service:
```
systemctl restart krb5kdc.service
```

2. Restricting Network Access:
If PKINIT cannot be disabled, restrict network access to port 88 (UDP/TCP) to trusted client subnets using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-source=192.168.1.0/24
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling PKINIT prevents users and services from using smart cards or X.509 certificate pre-authentication. Restricting network access prevents unlisted subnets from obtaining Kerberos tickets.

Warning: Restarting `krb5kdc.service` will cause a momentary interruption to active authentication requests.

vulnerabilities.title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request

Restrict network access to the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) ports (88 UDP/TCP) to trusted client networks, or disable the KDC service on systems not operating as identity controllers.

To stop and disable the KDC service on systems where it is not required:
systemctl stop krb5kdc
systemctl disable krb5kdc

To restrict network access to an authorized client subnet (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) using firewalld:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" service name="kerberos" accept'

Warning: Reloading firewall rules or stopping the KDC service will immediately terminate active Kerberos connections and fail in-flight ticket requests.

cwe.name: Unverified Password Change

notes.text: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because exploitation requires pre-existing, high-privilege authorization equivalent to delegated change-password rights over the targeted principal. Without explicit delegated permissions assigned through administrative ACLs or an authorization plugin, unprivileged or unauthenticated network callers cannot bypass key lockdown controls. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, accounts marked with the key lockdown attribute are sensitive and rarely granted delegated modification access to other users, limiting the blast radius of this flaw to specific non-default configurations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Audit Kerberos access controls to ensure delegated password-change permissions are not assigned over protected accounts, or restrict network reachability to the kpasswd service.

1. Review the administrative ACL file (typically `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl`) and remove entries granting `c` (change-password) permissions over principals configured with `+lockdown_keys`. Restart the Kerberos administration daemon to apply the change:
```
systemctl restart kadmin.service
```

2. If remote password changes are not required or should be restricted to trusted administration networks, remove the kpasswd service from the public firewall zone or configure rich rules to limit access to port 464:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=kpasswd
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Modifying ACL permissions will stop delegated operators from performing password changes on those targets. Restricting or blocking port 464 will prevent clients from performing network password changes via kpasswd. Restarting `kadmin.service` or reloading `firewalld` may cause a momentary interruption to active administrative sessions and network traffic.

Each failed request allocates client state that is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout, allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it is reclaimed.

notes.text: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause sustained memory exhaustion leading to a denial of service on reachable administrative endpoints without requiring valid credentials. It does not qualify for a Critical rating because the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution or compromise data integrity and confidentiality. On standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux installations, the affected kadmind service is not enabled by default and is typically confined to dedicated Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) environments.

notes.text: In MIT krb5 release 1.4 and later, an active network attacker can alter the arguments sent by a legitimate client to RPC services protected by RPCSEC_GSS, or cause return values to be sent in plain text.

notes.text: krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because it enables an on-path network attacker to compromise the integrity and confidentiality of administrative RPC sessions protected by RPCSEC_GSS. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, kadmind is not active by default and is typically confined to dedicated Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) systems. The risk is elevated when administrative endpoints are exposed to untrusted or transit networks where an active man-in-the-middle attacker can modify administrative commands or intercept sensitive responses in cleartext.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If remote administration of the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) is not required, stop and mask the kadmind service and manage the realm locally using kadmin.local:

```
systemctl stop kadmin.service
systemctl mask kadmin.service
```

If remote administration is required, restrict network access to the Kerberos administration port (port 749/tcp) to authorized administrator IP addresses or dedicated management subnets using firewalld:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=drop --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<ADMIN_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling the kadmind service prevents remote administrative operations via the kadmin client, requiring administrators to execute kadmin.local directly on the KDC host. Restricting or reloading firewall rules will disrupt unauthorized remote sessions and may momentarily interrupt active network connections during rule application.

notes.text: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.

notes.text: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity issue because remote unauthenticated attackers can cause excessive CPU consumption and degrade KDC availability without requiring valid credentials or user interaction. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, this impact specifically targets the krb5kdc daemon when listening for incoming TCP traffic from untrusted networks. Systems where the Kerberos Key Distribution Center is restricted to trusted subnets experience lower operational risk, and the flaw cannot be leveraged for unauthorized data disclosure or remote code execution.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict incoming TCP traffic on port 88 to trusted internal networks or authorized administrative hosts using firewalld.

1. Add a rich rule permitting TCP port 88 only from trusted networks (substitute with the appropriate network CIDR):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" port port="88" protocol="tcp" accept'

2. Ensure unauthenticated or public access to port 88/tcp is removed:
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=88/tcp

3. Apply the changes:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Applying firewall changes requires reloading firewalld, which may temporarily disrupt network traffic. Restricting TCP access will prevent clients outside the allowed network range from falling back to TCP for large Kerberos ticket exchanges.

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Kerberos is a network authentication system, which can improve the security of your network by eliminating the insecure practice of sending passwords over the network in unencrypted form. It allows clients and servers to authenticate to each other with the help of a trusted third party, the Kerberos key distribution center (KDC).

Security Fix(es):

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests (CVE-2026-112323)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup (CVE-2026-112322)

* krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries (CVE-2026-112314)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request (CVE-2026-71200)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths (CVE-2026-112321)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching (CVE-2026-112320)

* krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd (CVE-2026-107884)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation (CVE-2026-112319)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers (CVE-2026-112318)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path (CVE-2026-112317)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding (CVE-2026-119079)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure (CVE-2026-112316)

* krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification (CVE-2026-111423)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure (CVE-2026-112315)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests (CVE-2026-107708)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials (CVE-2026-107778)

* krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container (CVE-2026-71199)

* krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure (CVE-2026-118380)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun (CVE-2026-107364)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* Set PKINIT CMS signatureAlgorithm based on certificate public key type [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-278059)

* auth_gssapi_wrap_data xdr_bytes failure leak [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296018)

* xdr_bytes() does not free its allocation on partial decode failure [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296030)

* RPCSEC_GSS context lifecycle leaks [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296039)

* xdr_krb5_principal decode leak [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296051)

* process_chpw_request leak [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296062)

* Read overruns in GSSRPC svcauth_unix [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296073)

* Null dereference in KDC dispatch corner case [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296085)

* KDC DoS based on otherName value in PKINIT SAN code [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296103)

* Memory leak on krb5 gss_accept_sec_context() failure [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296119)

* KDC authdata filter does not catch KDC-issued types nested inside AD-IF-RELEVANT containers [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296134)

* Null dereference of principal names in krb5_rd_cred() [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-297007)

* Dereference of empty first credential list element in GSS mechanism [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-297015)

* Fix validation issues for trusted inputs [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299746)

* Skip expired keys when iterating over KEYRING ccache [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299747)

* Pass through null deleg_cred from SPNEGO to mech [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299748)

* Fix leaks on error in PKINIT signed-data creation [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299749)

* Fix hex key input handling in ktutil addent [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299750)

* Check reply length before V4 reply check [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299751)

* Fix memory leak in mpool_get() error paths [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299752)

* json: Correctly abort parse on invalid array [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299753)

* Prevent unsigned int overflow in iakerb_save_token() [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299754)

* Fix ksu memory leak in fcmd_resolve() [rhel-9.9.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299755)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to a complete denial of service across the authentication realm. In default Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations, PKINIT pre-authentication is not activated; exploitation strictly requires the administrator to have explicitly enabled PKINIT via `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` in the KDC configuration. Deployments operating with standard Kerberos authentication mechanisms and without PKINIT configured are unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable PKINIT on the KDC if certificate-based authentication is not required, or restrict network access to the KDC service using firewall rules.

1. Disabling PKINIT:
Edit `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf` and comment out or remove the `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` directives within the realm configuration:
```
# pkinit_identity = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.pem,/etc/krb5kdc/kdckey.pem
# pkinit_anchors = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/cacert.pem
```

Apply the changes by restarting the service:
```
systemctl restart krb5kdc.service
```

2. Restricting Network Access:
If PKINIT cannot be disabled, restrict network access to port 88 (UDP/TCP) to trusted client subnets using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-source=192.168.1.0/24
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling PKINIT prevents users and services from using smart cards or X.509 certificate pre-authentication. Restricting network access prevents unlisted subnets from obtaining Kerberos tickets.

Warning: Restarting `krb5kdc.service` will cause a momentary interruption to active authentication requests.

vulnerabilities.title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because an unauthenticated remote network attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to an immediate denial of service across the entire authentication realm. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux and related offerings, the KDC service is not enabled by default on standard deployments and is typically confined to dedicated identity management servers (such as FreeIPA or standalone KDCs). Standard endpoints and systems operating solely as Kerberos clients do not process incoming KDC requests and are not directly vulnerable to this service interruption.

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict network access to the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) ports (88 UDP/TCP) to trusted client networks, or disable the KDC service on systems not operating as identity controllers.

To stop and disable the KDC service on systems where it is not required:
systemctl stop krb5kdc
systemctl disable krb5kdc

To restrict network access to an authorized client subnet (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) using firewalld:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" service name="kerberos" accept'
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveat: Disabling the service or blocking network traffic prevents unlisted clients from obtaining Kerberos tickets, which will disrupt authentication and single sign-on services in the realm.

Warning: Reloading firewall rules or stopping the KDC service will immediately terminate active Kerberos connections and fail in-flight ticket requests.

cwe.name: Unverified Password Change

notes.text: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because exploitation requires pre-existing, high-privilege authorization equivalent to delegated change-password rights over the targeted principal. Without explicit delegated permissions assigned through administrative ACLs or an authorization plugin, unprivileged or unauthenticated network callers cannot bypass key lockdown controls. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, accounts marked with the key lockdown attribute are sensitive and rarely granted delegated modification access to other users, limiting the blast radius of this flaw to specific non-default configurations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Audit Kerberos access controls to ensure delegated password-change permissions are not assigned over protected accounts, or restrict network reachability to the kpasswd service.

1. Review the administrative ACL file (typically `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl`) and remove entries granting `c` (change-password) permissions over principals configured with `+lockdown_keys`. Restart the Kerberos administration daemon to apply the change:
```
systemctl restart kadmin.service
```

2. If remote password changes are not required or should be restricted to trusted administration networks, remove the kpasswd service from the public firewall zone or configure rich rules to limit access to port 464:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=kpasswd
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Modifying ACL permissions will stop delegated operators from performing password changes on those targets. Restricting or blocking port 464 will prevent clients from performing network password changes via kpasswd. Restarting `kadmin.service` or reloading `firewalld` may cause a momentary interruption to active administrative sessions and network traffic.

notes.text: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger authentication failures.

notes.text: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust system memory by repeatedly sending malformed authentication initialization requests over the network. In typical Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, exposure is limited to daemons processing legacy RPC authentication, specifically administrative services such as kadmind. While standard Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) authentication traffic is unaffected, exposing administrative services directly to untrusted networks enables remote denial of service without requiring valid credentials.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because it enables an on-path network attacker to compromise the integrity and confidentiality of administrative RPC sessions protected by RPCSEC_GSS. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, kadmind is not active by default and is typically confined to dedicated Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) systems. The risk is elevated when administrative endpoints are exposed to untrusted or transit networks where an active man-in-the-middle attacker can modify administrative commands or intercept sensitive responses in cleartext.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If remote administration of the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) is not required, stop and mask the kadmind service and manage the realm locally using kadmin.local:

```
systemctl stop kadmin.service
systemctl mask kadmin.service
```

If remote administration is required, restrict network access to the Kerberos administration port (port 749/tcp) to authorized administrator IP addresses or dedicated management subnets using firewalld:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=drop --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<ADMIN_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling the kadmind service prevents remote administrative operations via the kadmin client, requiring administrators to execute kadmin.local directly on the KDC host. Restricting or reloading firewall rules will disrupt unauthorized remote sessions and may momentarily interrupt active network connections during rule application.

notes.text: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity issue because remote unauthenticated attackers can cause excessive CPU consumption and degrade KDC availability without requiring valid credentials or user interaction. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, this impact specifically targets the krb5kdc daemon when listening for incoming TCP traffic from untrusted networks. Systems where the Kerberos Key Distribution Center is restricted to trusted subnets experience lower operational risk, and the flaw cannot be leveraged for unauthorized data disclosure or remote code execution.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict incoming TCP traffic on port 88 to trusted internal networks or authorized administrative hosts using firewalld.

1. Add a rich rule permitting TCP port 88 only from trusted networks (substitute with the appropriate network CIDR):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" port port="88" protocol="tcp" accept'

2. Ensure unauthenticated or public access to port 88/tcp is removed:
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=88/tcp

3. Apply the changes:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Applying firewall changes requires reloading firewalld, which may temporarily disrupt network traffic. Restricting TCP access will prevent clients outside the allowed network range from falling back to TCP for large Kerberos ticket exchanges.

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Kerberos is a network authentication system, which can improve the security of your network by eliminating the insecure practice of sending passwords over the network in unencrypted form. It allows clients and servers to authenticate to each other with the help of a trusted third party, the Kerberos key distribution center (KDC).

Security Fix(es):

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests (CVE-2026-112323)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup (CVE-2026-112322)

* krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries (CVE-2026-112314)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request (CVE-2026-71200)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths (CVE-2026-112321)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching (CVE-2026-112320)

* krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd (CVE-2026-107884)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation (CVE-2026-112319)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers (CVE-2026-112318)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path (CVE-2026-112317)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding (CVE-2026-119079)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure (CVE-2026-112316)

* krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification (CVE-2026-111423)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure (CVE-2026-112315)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests (CVE-2026-107708)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials (CVE-2026-107778)

* krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container (CVE-2026-71199)

* krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure (CVE-2026-118380)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun (CVE-2026-107364)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* Set PKINIT CMS signatureAlgorithm based on certificate public key type [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-278062)

* auth_gssapi_wrap_data xdr_bytes failure leak [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296011)

* xdr_bytes() does not free its allocation on partial decode failure [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296022)

* RPCSEC_GSS context lifecycle leaks [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296033)

* xdr_krb5_principal decode leak [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296044)

* process_chpw_request leak [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296055)

* Read overruns in GSSRPC svcauth_unix [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296066)

* Null dereference in KDC dispatch corner case [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296079)

* KDC DoS based on otherName value in PKINIT SAN code [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296093)

* Memory leak on krb5 gss_accept_sec_context() failure [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296111)

* KDC authdata filter does not catch KDC-issued types nested inside AD-IF-RELEVANT containers [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296126)

* Dereference of empty first credential list element in GSS mechanism [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296996)

* Null dereference of principal names in krb5_rd_cred() [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296999)

* Fix validation issues for trusted inputs [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299156)

* Skip expired keys when iterating over KEYRING ccache [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299157)

* Fix ksu memory leak in fcmd_resolve() [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299158)

* Prevent unsigned int overflow in iakerb_save_token() [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299159)

* json: Correctly abort parse on invalid array [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299160)

* Fix memory leak in mpool_get() error paths [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299161)

* Check reply length before V4 reply check [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299162)

* Fix hex key input handling in ktutil addent [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299163)

* Fix leaks on error in PKINIT signed-data creation [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299164)

* Pass through null deleg_cred from SPNEGO to mech [rhel-10.2.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299165)

Deployments that do not enforce authentication indicators on service principals are not exposed to this security policy bypass.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to a complete denial of service across the authentication realm. In default Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations, PKINIT pre-authentication is not activated; exploitation strictly requires the administrator to have explicitly enabled PKINIT via `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` in the KDC configuration. Deployments operating with standard Kerberos authentication mechanisms and without PKINIT configured are unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable PKINIT on the KDC if certificate-based authentication is not required, or restrict network access to the KDC service using firewall rules.

1. Disabling PKINIT:
Edit `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf` and comment out or remove the `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` directives within the realm configuration:
```
# pkinit_identity = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.pem,/etc/krb5kdc/kdckey.pem
# pkinit_anchors = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/cacert.pem
```

Apply the changes by restarting the service:
```
systemctl restart krb5kdc.service
```

2. Restricting Network Access:
If PKINIT cannot be disabled, restrict network access to port 88 (UDP/TCP) to trusted client subnets using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-source=192.168.1.0/24
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling PKINIT prevents users and services from using smart cards or X.509 certificate pre-authentication. Restricting network access prevents unlisted subnets from obtaining Kerberos tickets.

Warning: Restarting `krb5kdc.service` will cause a momentary interruption to active authentication requests.

vulnerabilities.title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Read

notes.text: In all released versions of MIT krb5, an unauthenticated attacker can cause a KDC process to perform a large read overrun, likely causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because an unauthenticated remote network attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to an immediate denial of service across the entire authentication realm. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux and related offerings, the KDC service is not enabled by default on standard deployments and is typically confined to dedicated identity management servers (such as FreeIPA or standalone KDCs). Standard endpoints and systems operating solely as Kerberos clients do not process incoming KDC requests and are not directly vulnerable to this service interruption.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict network access to the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) ports (88 UDP/TCP) to trusted client networks, or disable the KDC service on systems not operating as identity controllers.

To stop and disable the KDC service on systems where it is not required:
systemctl stop krb5kdc
systemctl disable krb5kdc

To restrict network access to an authorized client subnet (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) using firewalld:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" service name="kerberos" accept'
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveat: Disabling the service or blocking network traffic prevents unlisted clients from obtaining Kerberos tickets, which will disrupt authentication and single sign-on services in the realm.

Warning: Reloading firewall rules or stopping the KDC service will immediately terminate active Kerberos connections and fail in-flight ticket requests.

notes.text: A flaw was found in krb5. This vulnerability allows a compromised or malicious cross-realm trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) to cause a Denial of Service (DoS). By sending an S4U2Proxy delegation request containing a malformed client name within a Privilege Attribute Certificate (PAC), an attacker can trigger a NULL pointer dereference that crashes the KDC daemon, interrupting authentication services.

While the resulting NULL pointer dereference causes the krb5kdc daemon to crash and interrupt authentication services, standard deployments operating within a single realm or without cross-realm constrained delegation are unaffected. Furthermore, the issue cannot be triggered by unauthenticated network clients and does not allow code execution or data modification.

cwe.name: Unverified Password Change

notes.text: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because exploitation requires pre-existing, high-privilege authorization equivalent to delegated change-password rights over the targeted principal. Without explicit delegated permissions assigned through administrative ACLs or an authorization plugin, unprivileged or unauthenticated network callers cannot bypass key lockdown controls. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, accounts marked with the key lockdown attribute are sensitive and rarely granted delegated modification access to other users, limiting the blast radius of this flaw to specific non-default configurations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Audit Kerberos access controls to ensure delegated password-change permissions are not assigned over protected accounts, or restrict network reachability to the kpasswd service.

1. Review the administrative ACL file (typically `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl`) and remove entries granting `c` (change-password) permissions over principals configured with `+lockdown_keys`. Restart the Kerberos administration daemon to apply the change:
```
systemctl restart kadmin.service
```

2. If remote password changes are not required or should be restricted to trusted administration networks, remove the kpasswd service from the public firewall zone or configure rich rules to limit access to port 464:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=kpasswd
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Modifying ACL permissions will stop delegated operators from performing password changes on those targets. Restricting or blocking port 464 will prevent clients from performing network password changes via kpasswd. Restarting `kadmin.service` or reloading `firewalld` may cause a momentary interruption to active administrative sessions and network traffic.

Furthermore, triggering client-side memory exhaustion requires a continuous flood of malformed responses during an active transaction, without compromising data integrity or confidentiality.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If remote administration of the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) is not required, stop and mask the kadmind service and manage the realm locally using kadmin.local:

```
systemctl stop kadmin.service
systemctl mask kadmin.service
```

If remote administration is required, restrict network access to the Kerberos administration port (port 749/tcp) to authorized administrator IP addresses or dedicated management subnets using firewalld:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=drop --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<ADMIN_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling the kadmind service prevents remote administrative operations via the kadmin client, requiring administrators to execute kadmin.local directly on the KDC host. Restricting or reloading firewall rules will disrupt unauthorized remote sessions and may momentarily interrupt active network connections during rule application.

notes.text: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.

notes.text: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity issue because remote unauthenticated attackers can cause excessive CPU consumption and degrade KDC availability without requiring valid credentials or user interaction. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, this impact specifically targets the krb5kdc daemon when listening for incoming TCP traffic from untrusted networks. Systems where the Kerberos Key Distribution Center is restricted to trusted subnets experience lower operational risk, and the flaw cannot be leveraged for unauthorized data disclosure or remote code execution.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict incoming TCP traffic on port 88 to trusted internal networks or authorized administrative hosts using firewalld.

1. Add a rich rule permitting TCP port 88 only from trusted networks (substitute with the appropriate network CIDR):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" port port="88" protocol="tcp" accept'

2. Ensure unauthenticated or public access to port 88/tcp is removed:
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=88/tcp

3. Apply the changes:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Applying firewall changes requires reloading firewalld, which may temporarily disrupt network traffic. Restricting TCP access will prevent clients outside the allowed network range from falling back to TCP for large Kerberos ticket exchanges.

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Kerberos is a network authentication system, which can improve the security of your network by eliminating the insecure practice of sending passwords over the network in unencrypted form. It allows clients and servers to authenticate to each other with the help of a trusted third party, the Kerberos key distribution center (KDC).

Security Fix(es):

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests (CVE-2026-112323)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup (CVE-2026-112322)

* krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries (CVE-2026-112314)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request (CVE-2026-71200)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths (CVE-2026-112321)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching (CVE-2026-112320)

* krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd (CVE-2026-107884)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation (CVE-2026-112319)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers (CVE-2026-112318)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path (CVE-2026-112317)

* krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding (CVE-2026-119079)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure (CVE-2026-112316)

* krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification (CVE-2026-111423)

* krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure (CVE-2026-112315)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests (CVE-2026-107708)

* krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials (CVE-2026-107778)

* krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container (CVE-2026-71199)

* krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure (CVE-2026-118380)

* krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun (CVE-2026-107364)

Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):

* Set PKINIT CMS signatureAlgorithm based on certificate public key type [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-278063)

* auth_gssapi_wrap_data xdr_bytes failure leak [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296012)

* xdr_bytes() does not free its allocation on partial decode failure [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296023)

* RPCSEC_GSS context lifecycle leaks [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296034)

* xdr_krb5_principal decode leak [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296045)

* process_chpw_request leak [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296056)

* Read overruns in GSSRPC svcauth_unix [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296067)

* Null dereference in KDC dispatch corner case [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296081)

* KDC DoS based on otherName value in PKINIT SAN code [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296095)

* Memory leak on krb5 gss_accept_sec_context() failure [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296112)

* KDC authdata filter does not catch KDC-issued types nested inside AD-IF-RELEVANT containers [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296127)

* Dereference of empty first credential list element in GSS mechanism [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-296997)

* Null dereference of principal names in krb5_rd_cred() [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-297000)

* Fix validation issues for trusted inputs [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299144)

* Skip expired keys when iterating over KEYRING ccache [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299145)

* Pass through null deleg_cred from SPNEGO to mech [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299146)

* Fix leaks on error in PKINIT signed-data creation [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299147)

* Fix hex key input handling in ktutil addent [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299148)

* Check reply length before V4 reply check [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299149)

* Fix memory leak in mpool_get() error paths [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299150)

* json: Correctly abort parse on invalid array [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299151)

* Prevent unsigned int overflow in iakerb_save_token() [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299152)

* Fix ksu memory leak in fcmd_resolve() [rhel-10.3.z] (JIRA:RHEL-299153)

Deployments that do not enforce authentication indicators on service principals are not exposed to this security policy bypass.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to a complete denial of service across the authentication realm. In default Red Hat Enterprise Linux configurations, PKINIT pre-authentication is not activated; exploitation strictly requires the administrator to have explicitly enabled PKINIT via `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` in the KDC configuration. Deployments operating with standard Kerberos authentication mechanisms and without PKINIT configured are unaffected.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable PKINIT on the KDC if certificate-based authentication is not required, or restrict network access to the KDC service using firewall rules.

1. Disabling PKINIT:
Edit `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf` and comment out or remove the `pkinit_identity` and `pkinit_anchors` directives within the realm configuration:
```
# pkinit_identity = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.pem,/etc/krb5kdc/kdckey.pem
# pkinit_anchors = FILE:/etc/krb5kdc/cacert.pem
```

Apply the changes by restarting the service:
```
systemctl restart krb5kdc.service
```

2. Restricting Network Access:
If PKINIT cannot be disabled, restrict network access to port 88 (UDP/TCP) to trusted client subnets using firewalld:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=internal --add-source=192.168.1.0/24
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling PKINIT prevents users and services from using smart cards or X.509 certificate pre-authentication. Restricting network access prevents unlisted subnets from obtaining Kerberos tickets.

Warning: Restarting `krb5kdc.service` will cause a momentary interruption to active authentication requests.

vulnerabilities.title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Read

notes.text: In all released versions of MIT krb5, an unauthenticated attacker can cause a KDC process to perform a large read overrun, likely causing the process to terminate.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because an unauthenticated remote network attacker can crash the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) daemon, leading to an immediate denial of service across the entire authentication realm. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux and related offerings, the KDC service is not enabled by default on standard deployments and is typically confined to dedicated identity management servers (such as FreeIPA or standalone KDCs). Standard endpoints and systems operating solely as Kerberos clients do not process incoming KDC requests and are not directly vulnerable to this service interruption.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict network access to the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) ports (88 UDP/TCP) to trusted client networks, or disable the KDC service on systems not operating as identity controllers.

To stop and disable the KDC service on systems where it is not required:
systemctl stop krb5kdc
systemctl disable krb5kdc

To restrict network access to an authorized client subnet (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24) using firewalld:
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service=kerberos
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" service name="kerberos" accept'
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveat: Disabling the service or blocking network traffic prevents unlisted clients from obtaining Kerberos tickets, which will disrupt authentication and single sign-on services in the realm.

Warning: Reloading firewall rules or stopping the KDC service will immediately terminate active Kerberos connections and fail in-flight ticket requests.

notes.text: A flaw was found in krb5. This vulnerability allows a compromised or malicious cross-realm trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) to cause a Denial of Service (DoS). While the resulting NULL pointer dereference causes the krb5kdc daemon to crash and interrupt authentication services, standard deployments operating within a single realm or without cross-realm constrained delegation are unaffected. Furthermore, the issue cannot be triggered by unauthenticated network clients and does not allow code execution or data modification.

cwe.name: Unverified Password Change

notes.text: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because exploitation requires pre-existing, high-privilege authorization equivalent to delegated change-password rights over the targeted principal. Without explicit delegated permissions assigned through administrative ACLs or an authorization plugin, unprivileged or unauthenticated network callers cannot bypass key lockdown controls. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, accounts marked with the key lockdown attribute are sensitive and rarely granted delegated modification access to other users, limiting the blast radius of this flaw to specific non-default configurations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Audit Kerberos access controls to ensure delegated password-change permissions are not assigned over protected accounts, or restrict network reachability to the kpasswd service.

1. Review the administrative ACL file (typically `/var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl`) and remove entries granting `c` (change-password) permissions over principals configured with `+lockdown_keys`. Restart the Kerberos administration daemon to apply the change:
```
systemctl restart kadmin.service
```

2. If remote password changes are not required or should be restricted to trusted administration networks, remove the kpasswd service from the public firewall zone or configure rich rules to limit access to port 464:
```
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-service=kpasswd
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Warning: Modifying ACL permissions will stop delegated operators from performing password changes on those targets. Restricting or blocking port 464 will prevent clients from performing network password changes via kpasswd. Restarting `kadmin.service` or reloading `firewalld` may cause a momentary interruption to active administrative sessions and network traffic.

vulnerabilities.title: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

If remote administration of the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) is not required, stop and mask the kadmind service and manage the realm locally using kadmin.local:

```
systemctl stop kadmin.service
systemctl mask kadmin.service
```

If remote administration is required, restrict network access to the Kerberos administration port (port 749/tcp) to authorized administrator IP addresses or dedicated management subnets using firewalld:

```
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=drop --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-source=<ADMIN_SUBNET>
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --add-port=749/tcp
firewall-cmd --reload
```

Caveats:
Disabling the kadmind service prevents remote administrative operations via the kadmin client, requiring administrators to execute kadmin.local directly on the KDC host. Restricting or reloading firewall rules will disrupt unauthorized remote sessions and may momentarily interrupt active network connections during rule application.

In Red Hat Enterprise Linux environments, this impact specifically targets the krb5kdc daemon when listening for incoming TCP traffic from untrusted networks. Systems where the Kerberos Key Distribution Center is restricted to trusted subnets experience lower operational risk, and the flaw cannot be leveraged for unauthorized data disclosure or remote code execution.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Restrict incoming TCP traffic on port 88 to trusted internal networks or authorized administrative hosts using firewalld.

1. Add a rich rule permitting TCP port 88 only from trusted networks (substitute with the appropriate network CIDR):
firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.1.0/24" port port="88" protocol="tcp" accept'

2. Ensure unauthenticated or public access to port 88/tcp is removed:
firewall-cmd --permanent --remove-port=88/tcp

3. Apply the changes:
firewall-cmd --reload

Warning: Applying firewall changes requires reloading firewalld, which may temporarily disrupt network traffic. Restricting TCP access will prevent clients outside the allowed network range from falling back to TCP for large Kerberos ticket exchanges.

notes.text: A flaw was found in krb5. This vulnerability allows a compromised or malicious cross-realm trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) to cause a Denial of Service (DoS). By sending an S4U2Proxy delegation request containing a malformed client name within a Privilege Attribute Certificate (PAC), an attacker can trigger a NULL pointer dereference that crashes the KDC daemon, interrupting authentication services.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact because successful exploitation requires an established cross-realm trust relationship and a compromised or rogue remote Key Distribution Center (KDC) sending an S4U2Proxy delegation request. While the resulting NULL pointer dereference causes the krb5kdc daemon to crash and interrupt authentication services, standard deployments operating within a single realm or without cross-realm constrained delegation are unaffected. Furthermore, the issue cannot be triggered by unauthenticated network clients and does not allow code execution or data modification.

However, the flaw does not facilitate arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, or unauthorized disclosure of confidential system data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in BuildKit. A malicious BuildKit client or frontend can craft a specially designed request, leading to the BuildKit daemon crashing. This vulnerability results in a denial of service (DoS), making the BuildKit service unavailable.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/moby/buildkit: BuildKit: Denial of Service via malicious client request
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: BuildKit is used by several Red Hat products to build container images. This issue allows a malicious BuildKit frontend or client to cause the BuildKit build process to crash. Exploiting this issue requires the ability to supply a build definition (for example, a Dockerfile specifying a custom #syntax frontend) to a BuildKit-based build; it does not allow remote code execution or exposure of data. The issue is fixed upstream in BuildKit version 0.31.2. Red Hat Hardened Images (Buildah, Podman, and Trivy) has already shipped the fixed version. Other affected Red Hat products are being assessed and will ship the fixed version of BuildKit in upcoming releases.
notes.title: Statement

Before you apply this update, make sure all previously released errata that are relevant to your system are applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Avoid building container images using BuildKit frontends from untrusted sources. A BuildKit frontend is typically specified using a "# syntax" directive at the top of a Dockerfile, or with the "--frontend" option to the "buildctl build" command. notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. The `qs.stringify` function, responsible for serializing objects, does not properly validate the `isBuffer` property of an object's constructor before attempting to invoke it. An unauthenticated attacker can provide specially crafted input that, when processed and then serialized by `qs.stringify`, triggers a `TypeError`. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS), causing affected applications to return a 500 error or, in certain scenarios, terminate the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: qs: qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Podman. When a container image with checkpoint annotations is executed using the podman run command, Podman treats the image as a restored checkpoint and ignores user-specified sandboxing options, such as dropped privileges. An attacker can exploit this issue by enticing a user to run a specially crafted image, leading to a container sandbox bypass and potential execution with elevated system privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: podman: podman: The `podman run` command can be instructed to disable almost all sandboxing - including user-requested sandboxing - by image annotation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important severity impact for Red Hat environments because running a malicious image can completely circumvent expected confinement boundaries and grant unexpected privileges to a container, compromising host integrity. Under default configurations, container execution relies on enforced sandboxing limits and security flags supplied by the operator. However, if an image embeds specific checkpoint metadata, the runtime automatically prioritizes the checkpoint configuration over explicit command-line restrictions, silently omitting requested security controls. Exploitation requires an operator or automated workflow to launch an untrusted image; environments that execute only vetted container workloads from trusted registries remain at reduced operational risk.

notes.text: A flaw was found in PyJWT. Exploitation occurs when consuming applications configure token verification to accept both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms simultaneously, allowing an asymmetric public key to be mishandled as a symmetric secret. Deployments that strictly enforce a single algorithm type or validate tokens using JSON Web Key sets do not permit this algorithm confusion and remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Quay where the robot account listing function constructs a SQL LIKE pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard metacharacters. An attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore character can match and retrieve robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens from other tenants' namespaces, leading to cross-tenant credential theft and unauthorized image operations.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: quay: quay: SQL LIKE wildcard injection in robot listing leaks cross-tenant robot tokens
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated Critical because it lets an authenticated attacker break tenant isolation in multi-tenant Quay deployments. By creating a namespace whose name contains an underscore that collides with an existing one, the attacker causes the underscore to act as a single-character SQL LIKE wildcard, matching the victim's namespace. This allows the attacker to list and steal the victim's robot account tokens, then use them to read, push, or overwrite that tenant's container images. No elevated privileges or victim interaction are required. In OpenShift environments where Quay serves as the integrated container registry, stolen robot credentials can be used to inject malicious images into CI/CD pipelines, putting the container supply chain across production clusters at risk. Multi-tenant Quay deployments are common in enterprises sharing a registry across teams and in service providers hosting multiple customer organizations.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Image Composer (MIC) file. When an application attempts to count or extract frames from the malicious image, an improper state reset triggers an infinite loop. This non-advancing loop consumes excessive CPU resources and can hang application worker processes indefinitely.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via infinite loop during crafted MIC image parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can induce an infinite loop, exhausting worker CPU resources and resulting in a denial of service for applications handling untrusted image data. Within Red Hat environments, Pillow is deployed across numerous container images, machine learning frameworks, and automated backend services. Exploitation requires the optional olefile dependency to be present to register the Microsoft Image Composer format handler, and specifically targets workflows that query frame counts or process multi-frame images. Environments that do not inspect frame counts or do not have olefile installed are not vulnerable.
notes.title: Statement
